# 📋 NCLEX Study & Preparation To-Do List

---

## **Phase 1: Planning & Setup (Weeks 1–2)**
- [ ] Determine your exam date and register with **Pearson VUE**
- [ ] Apply for licensure through your **state Board of Nursing**
- [ ] Obtain your **ATT (Authorization to Test)**
- [ ] Choose a primary review resource (e.g., UWorld, Archer, Hurst, Kaplan, Mark Klimek)
- [ ] Create a realistic study schedule (8–12 weeks recommended)
- [ ] Set daily/weekly question goals (minimum **75–150 questions/day**)
- [ ] Join NCLEX study groups (Reddit, Facebook, Discord)

---

## **Phase 2: Content Review (Weeks 2–6)**
- [ ] **Pharmacology** – Learn top drug classes, suffixes, side effects, and nursing interventions
- [ ] **Med-Surg** – Focus on priority conditions (heart failure, diabetes, renal failure, COPD, etc.)
- [ ] **Maternal/Newborn** – Stages of labor, complications, newborn assessment
- [ ] **Pediatrics** – Growth & development milestones, common childhood illnesses
- [ ] **Psych/Mental Health** – Therapeutic communication, crisis intervention, medications
- [ ] **Fundamentals** – Infection control, safety, basic care, ABCs, Maslow's hierarchy
- [ ] **Leadership/Delegation** – Scope of practice (RN vs. LPN vs. UAP), priority & delegation rules
- [ ] **Lab values** – Memorize critical lab values (K⁺, Na⁺, BUN, creatinine, WBC, Hgb, etc.)
- [ ] Review **fluid & electrolyte imbalances**
- [ ] Review **acid-base balance** (ABGs interpretation)

---

## **Phase 3: Question Practice & Critical Thinking (Weeks 4–10)**
- [ ] Complete **entire UWorld or Archer question bank** (read ALL rationales)
- [ ] Track weak areas and review content for each missed question
- [ ] Practice **SATA (Select All That Apply)** questions daily
- [ ] Practice **prioritization & delegation** questions daily
- [ ] Practice **drag-and-drop, hot spot, and fill-in-the-blank** question types
- [ ] Focus on **NGN (Next Generation NCLEX)** case study and clinical judgment questions
- [ ] Understand the **Clinical Judgment Measurement Model (CJMM)** – 6 cognitive skills
- [ ] Aim for consistent scores of **56%+ on UWorld** or **"high" on readiness assessments**

---

## **Phase 4: High-Yield Review (Weeks 8–11)**
- [ ] Listen to **Mark Klimek audio lectures** (prioritization, pharm, delegation, psych)
- [ ] Review mnemonics and memory aids
- [ ] Make flashcards for weak areas (or use Anki/Quizlet)
- [ ] Re-do all **incorrectly answered questions**
- [ ] Review **infection control** – airborne, droplet, contact precautions
- [ ] Review **emergency procedures** – CPR updates, stroke protocol, chest tube management
- [ ] Review **patient positioning** (Trendelenburg, high Fowler's, side-lying, etc.)
- [ ] Review **immunization schedules**
- [ ] Know your **ABCs, Maslow's Hierarchy, and Nursing Process** for prioritization

---

## **Phase 5: Readiness Assessments (Week 10–11)**
- [ ] Take a **UWorld Self-Assessment** (1 or 2)
- [ ] Take an **Archer readiness assessment** (aim for 4+ "very high" in a row)
- [ ] Take the **Kaplan readiness exam** if available
- [ ] Evaluate results and focus final review on weak areas
- [ ] If scoring well → schedule your test. If not → delay and study more.

---

## **Phase 6: Final Week Before Exam**
- [ ] Do **light review only** – no heavy content cramming
- [ ] Review quick-reference sheets (lab values, drug suffixes, precautions)
- [ ] Do **50–75 practice questions/day** max to stay sharp
- [ ] Visit the testing center location (know where to go/park)
- [ ] Prepare your **valid ID** (check Pearson VUE requirements)
- [ ] Get proper sleep (7–8 hours the night before)
- [ ] Prepare comfort items (snack, water for breaks, layers of clothing)

---

## **Phase 7: Exam Day**
- [ ] Eat a good breakfast
- [ ] Arrive early (30 minutes before appointment)
- [ ] Bring **valid, unexpired government-issued ID**
- [ ] Stay calm – use deep breathing if anxious
- [ ] Read every question carefully – **what is the question ACTUALLY asking?**
- [ ] Use **ABC's → Safety → Maslow's → Nursing Process** to eliminate answers
- [ ] Don't rush – take breaks if needed
- [ ] Trust your preparation

---

## **Phase 8: Post-Exam**
- [ ] Try the **Pearson VUE Trick (PVT)** after ~2 hours for an unofficial result
- [ ] Purchase **Quick Results** from Pearson VUE after 48 hours ($7.95)
- [ ] Wait for official results from your state Board of Nursing
- [ ] 🎉 **CELEBRATE when you pass!**

---

## **Key Resources Checklist**
| Resource | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **UWorld** | #1 question bank |
| **Archer Review** | Affordable alternative Qbank + readiness exams |
| **Mark Klimek** | Audio lectures for prioritization & high-yield topics |
| **Hurst Review** | Excellent content review course |
| **Kaplan** | Question trainers & decision tree method |
| **Simple Nursing (YouTube)** | Visual/animated content review |
| **RegisteredNurseRN (YouTube)** | Detailed topic breakdowns |

---

> **💡 Golden Rules:**
> - The NCLEX tests **critical thinking**, not memorization
> - Think: **"What is the SAFEST thing to do FIRST?"**
> - The answer is almost never "call the doctor" first
> - **Assessment before intervention** (unless it's an emergency)
> - You are the **nurse**, not the doctor – stay in your scope
> - **Never delegate assessment, teaching, or evaluation** to a UAP

Good luck — you've got this! 🩺✨
